assumptions.choice: use close for 'price first goes below the 0.618 level'
assumptions.reason: spec explicitly offers 'close or low' as an either/or choice for this condition; close was picked for consistency with condition 3 which also uses close
spec says 'closes back above', which literally reads as strictly greater than

assumptions.choice: 'retracements from A to B' implemented as level(ratio) = B - (B-A)*ratio
assumptions.reason: standard Fibonacci-tool convention where the endpoint (B) is 0% and the ratio measures distance back toward the start point (A); applied to both the stated uptrend (low->high) and 'otherwise' (high->low) branches

assumptions.choice: used index of first occurrence (list.index()) of the max/min within the trailing 200-bar window to decide whether swing high occurs before swing low
assumptions.reason: backtrader has no built-in 'index of extreme' indicator; manual scan over data.high/low.get(size=200) was the closest literal way to determine temporal order, with ties broken by earliest occurrence

assumptions.topic: state-machine reset scope ('only once per swing range')
assumptions.choice: reset the 3-stage state machine to stage 0 whenever the computed (swing_high, swing_low) pair changes from the prior bar; once a full entry sequence fires (stage 3) it stays latched until the swing range changes, blocking further entries for that same range
assumptions.reason: spec requires the sequence to occur 'only once per swing range' but does not define range identity explicitly; equality of the swing high/low pair was used as the literal proxy for 'same swing range'

assumptions.choice: implemented the explicitly given example: close >= Highest(high, 20), rather than a trailing stop
assumptions.reason: spec offers a trailing stop as an alternative ('if preferred'), but the N-bar local high example is stated first and precisely, with an explicit parameter (N=20), so it was chosen as the literal, deterministic rule

assumptions.topic: state-machine progression while in a position
assumptions.choice: stage transitions (0->1->2) only evaluated while flat (no open position); while a position is open only the exit rule is checked
assumptions.reason: canonical default disallows pyramiding/re-entry while a position is open, and since a completed entry always advances the machine to a terminal stage 3, this has no effect on signal generation but keeps entry/exit logic cleanly separated
